newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest hog prices steady-up $0.50 - trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest hog prices steady-up $0.50 - trade.

text.p: U.S. Midwest cash hogs early Tuesday sold steady to $0.50 per cwt higher amid strong packer demand and light marketings, livestock dealers said.

Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs traded in light volume at $55.50 to $57.00 in the country and $57.50 to $58.00 at plants. Hog movement was slowed, but not stopped, by overnight snowfall of one to five inches through central Iowa, buyers said.
Illinois prices were steady at $55.50 to $57.50 in the country and $58.50 at plants. Indiana country stations were paying $55.00 and plants were paying $57.50 to $58.00.
Ohio hog buyers said prices were fully steady at $53.00 to $54.00 in the country and $56.00 at plants. Trading was light.

Thin support was attributed to moderate pork movement Monday at mixed prices, with most of the demand coming from processors, according to USDA. Retail pork demand was slow and offerings were light to moderate, USDA said.
